follow the instructions to colour each decade of this rosary beads to create your own mission rosary. joyful mysteries monday, saturday sorrowful mysteries tuesday, friday luminous mysteries thursday glorious mysteries wednesday, sunday *the annunciation *the visitation *the nativity *the presentation *the finding in the temple *the agony in the garden *the scourging at the pillar *the crowning with thorns *the carrying of the cross *the crucifixion *the baptism of jesus *the wedding feast at cana *the proclamation of the kingdom *the transfiguration *the institution of the eucharist *the resurrection *the ascension *the descent of the holy spirit *the assumption *the coronation vol. 36 no. 32 11th october 2026 twenty eighth sunday in ordinary time this week’s readings first reading: isaiah 25:6-10a responsorial psalm: psalm 23 second reading: philippians 4:12-14, 19-20 gospel: matthew 22:1-14 or 22:1-10 key theme: god’s invitation to joy focus: faith and readiness summary: god welcomes everyone to his feast. he p rovides comfort, strength, and hope. we must accept his invitation with ready h earts. challenge: trust god in both plenty and need. res pond to his call with faith. live in a way that shows you are ready. action step: welcome someone who feels left out t his week. verse to remember: “invite to the feast whomever you find.” (matthew 2 2:9) sunday's scriptures the feast is ready god does not wait for us to be worthy before inviting us to his table. through isaiah, he promises a banquet for peoples, where death is destroyed and every tear wiped away. in the gospel, the king sends his serva nts to the crossroads: “invite everyone you can find.” the feast is ready— but we must come clothed in the grace he gives, not in our own self- sufficiency. st paul, even in prison, learned that christ is enough: “there is nothing i cannot master with the help of the one who gives me strength.” at mass, we taste that heavenly banquet. let us accept the invitation, put on christ, and bring others to the feast. come —everything is ready. world mission sunday – 18 october 2026 sunday, 18th october, the church marks 100 years o f world mission sunday, with the theme “missionaries of hope among all peoples.” it is the holy father’s official day of prayer and support for ove rseas missions, coordinated in ireland by mission ireland. how we can help: - pray for missionaries and young churches. - offer small sacrifices and acts of kindness. - give generously to the mission sunday collection/ envelopes. your support helps bring the gospel, education, hea lthcare and pastoral care to communities in need. please give what you can. thank you. mooncoin

please let us know who will be there on the night to present the candle candles will be supplied by the parish. major restoration of the church tower in recent times it has become apparent that there some significant structural problems in the tower of holy trinity church durrow. the wooden louvres (slanted beams) on all four sides of the tower are rotting, and each is framed in steel. these present a significant health and safety risk. when the tower was examined earlier in the summer other major difoculties with the pointing of stonework were also identified. the upshot of all this is that some major restoration work is necessary and as a matter of urgency. the work is scheduled to begin on monday next, 19th of october and will take approximately four to six weeks. the doors across the front of the church will remain locked during the work and entrance to the church will be through the side aisle doors only. the front of the church and the tower is a building site and therefore a health and safety risk. i realise this presents an inconvenience, but i ask for your consideration and cooperation. i am grateful to the parish finance committee and the diocesan authorities who have worked with me to address this problem. together with other necessary works to repair the lightning conductors on the church carried out earlier in the year, this major repair job will cost in the region of €90,000. your ongoing weekly financial support for the parish through the blue envelope collection was never more needed and appreciated. fr. martin best wishes to st brigid’s camogie
